title: codelaw configuration
description: codelaw.toml, [tool.codelaw] in pyproject.toml, or "codelaw" in package.json (SR-CONFIG). Every key names the one record that defines it in x-codelaw-record.

remap.description: Each severity of a finding in these files mapped to another, or to off; applied last, after the baseline. Never remaps codelaw/* diagnostics.

globs.description: Globs relative to the folder of the config that declares them.

size.description: Bytes, or a string such as "1 MiB" or "512MB".

duration.description: Seconds, or a string such as "5s" or "500ms".

ruleSetting.description: A severity, or a severity, options, a lowered fix and the reason a rule is off.

fix.description: Lower the rule's fix (SR-LAW-4 decision 16): `suggest` stops `codelaw fix`, save and the agent hook applying it; `manual` stops every surface applying it. At or below the rule's own rung; raising is a config error.

reason.description: Why the rule is turned off (SR-CONFIG decision 11c): only with `severity = "off"`. Mandatory when `[rules] require_reason` is true.

rules.description: Severity and options per rule id (`<namespace>/<name>`).

rootRules.description: The top-level `[rules]`: severity and options per rule id (`<namespace>/<name>`), and `require_reason`.

require_reason.description: Every rule entry in the project's config that sets `severity = "off"` must carry a `reason`; one that does not is a `codelaw/off-without-reason` finding (SR-CONFIG decision 11c). Root config only.

extends.description: Presets: `codelaw:<namespace>/<preset>`, or team packs as `npm:`, `pypi:` or `path:`. Root config only.

languages.description: The languages checked; all of them when absent. The innermost config that sets it wins.

rules_dir.description: The local rules folder; `.codelaw/rules` by default. Root config only.

scope.description: Named groups of files with their own rule settings, applied in file order after [rules]; a preset may ship one (`tests`), and the project's of the same name extends it. A name is lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`; `default` is reserved.

overrides.description: Deprecated: write [scope.<name>]. Each entry loads as scope `override-<n>` with a warning; goes in the next minor release.

profile.description: Named sets of rules and scopes, applied after the configs' own: `ci` when CI is set, `local` otherwise, or --profile / CODELAW_PROFILE. Root config only.

profiles.description: Deprecated: write [profile.<name>]. Loads with a warning; goes in the next minor release.

root.description: Make this folder a separate project with its own graph and baseline.

requires.description: A version range, e.g. ">=0.4"; an older codelaw refuses to run.

preview.description: Run preview rules (SR-RULE-PACKS decision 9). Root config only.

allow_pack_fixers.description: Packs whose external fixers may run (SR-RULE-PACKS decision 12). Root config only.

files.description: Discovery, encoding and size (SR-ARCHITECTURE decisions 7 and 10). Root config only.

follow_symlinks.description: Follow symlinks during discovery; off by default.

generated_markers.description: Markers besides `@generated` that mark a file generated.

lint_generated.description: Check generated files too; off by default.

max_file_size.description: Larger files are skipped; 1 MiB by default.

cache.description: The result cache (SR-CACHE decisions 3, 6 and 9). Root config only.

enabled.description: On by default; `--no-cache` turns it off for one run.

fix.description: The fix pipeline (SR-ARCHITECTURE decision 18). Root config only.

external_timeout.description: Per file, for an external fixer; 5 s by default.

on_edit.description: Whether every rule's `auto` fix runs on save and from the agent hook (SR-CONFIG decision 11e), below the per-rule entries. Unset, each rule keeps its own default (SR-RULE-FORMAT decision 2b).

multi_file.description: Whether a fix may edit several files (SR-MULTI-FILE-FIXES decision 3): `auto` (the default), `suggest` keeps each a diff, `off` offers none.

lint.description: The linter (SR-LINTER decision 3). Root config only.

tagged_templates.description: Lint css`…` and html`…` tagged templates as CSS and HTML; off by default.

ignore_aliases.description: Read these tools' line suppressions (eslint-disable-next-line / eslint-disable-line, # noqa, biome-ignore) as codelaw-ignore, through each rule's ported_from; none by default. `codelaw migrate` turns its tool's on.

lint_code_blocks.description: Lint fenced code blocks with their own language's rules; off by default.

format.description: The formatter (SR-FORMATTER). Its keys are validated once the formatter is built.

graph.description: The project graph (SR-PROJECT-GRAPH). Its keys are validated once the graph is built.

baseline.description: The baseline (SR-BASELINE). Its keys are validated once the baseline is built.

deprecation.description: The policy of a symbol marked deprecated in code (JSDoc `@deprecated`, PEP 702) that `.codelaw/deprecations.toml` does not list (SR-BASELINE decision 6). Root config only.

until.description: Deprecated alias of `expires`, for one minor release: the last allowed day, read as `expires` the day after (SR-BASELINE decision 9).

expires.description: The first day, YYYY-MM-DD, a grandfathered use is no longer allowed (SR-BASELINE decision 9).

warn_from.description: From this date, YYYY-MM-DD, the grandfathering warns that it expires; it wins over `warn_days`.

warn_days.description: Days of warning before `expires`; `[exceptions] warn_days` when unset.

on_touch.description: What a grandfathered use becomes when its file is touched.

exceptions.description: Dated exceptions: baseline entries, deprecations-registry entries and inline `codelaw-ignore` comments (SR-BASELINE decision 9). Root config only.

require_expiry.description: Every exception must carry `expires`; one without is an error, `codelaw/exception-without-expiry`.

warn_days.description: How many days before its `expires` an exception becomes a warning, `codelaw/expiring-exception`.

coverage.description: The test rules of new code, `graph/untested-function` and `graph/function-coverage` (SR-PROJECT-GRAPH decision 9). Root config only.

report.description: The lcov report `graph/function-coverage` reads, relative to the config file; `--coverage` wins.

scope.description: `all`: every new or edited function; `public`: only exported ones (JS/TS), or ones with no leading `_` or in `__all__` (Python).

min.description: The least line coverage, in percent, of each new or edited function.

mode.description: `function`: one finding per function under `min`; `patch`: one finding when all new and edited functions' lines together are under `min`.

require_report.description: No coverage report is an error, not a skip.

on_no_change_set.description: `skip`: with no change set nothing is judged; `all`: every function is judged (a baseline roll-out).

ignore_names.description: A regular expression: functions whose name matches it are never judged.

ignore.description: Deprecated: the old spelling of `[codelawignore]`, read until the next minor release (SR-BASELINE decision 12).

require_expiry.description: Every line says `expires=…` or `forever`; one without is `codelaw/incomplete-ignore`.

require_on_touch.description: Every line that is not `forever` says `on_touch=…`; one without is `codelaw/incomplete-ignore`.

on_touch.description: What an edit does to a line that does not say: `error` revokes it, `warn` revokes it as warnings, `keep` keeps it.

on_touch_scope.description: What counts as an edit for a line that does not say: `file`, any change to the file; `function`, the function's tokens changed.

codelawignore.description: What every `.codelawignore` line must carry, and the defaults of a line; the file exempts named files or functions from any rule (SR-BASELINE decision 12). Root config only.

require_expiry.description: Every line says `expires=…` or `forever`; one without is `codelaw/incomplete-ignore`.

require_on_touch.description: Every line that is not `forever` says `on_touch=…`; one without is `codelaw/incomplete-ignore`.

on_touch.description: What an edit does to a line that does not say: `error` revokes it, `warn` revokes it as warnings, `keep` keeps it.

on_touch_scope.description: What counts as an edit for a line that does not say: `file`, any change to the file; `function`, the function's tokens changed.

css.description: CSS Modules: which stylesheets are modules, and how the bundler turns a class name into `styles.x`. Read by the `css-modules/*` rules and the project graph. Root config only.

modules.description: Globs of CSS Module stylesheets besides `*.module.css` and `*.module.scss`, from the project root.

modules_convention.description: css-loader's `localsConvention`: how a class such as `.btn-primary` is reached from JavaScript. `asIs`: `styles["btn-primary"]`; `camelCase`: that and `styles.btnPrimary`; `camelCaseOnly`: only `styles.btnPrimary`; `dashes` and `dashesOnly`: dashes become camel case, other characters stay.

codeowners.description: CODEOWNERS coverage (SR-RULE-PACKS decision 16): where the file is and what it may leave out. Read by `data/codeowners-coverage`. Root config only.

path.description: The CODEOWNERS file, from the project root. By default the first of `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, `docs/CODEOWNERS` and `.gitlab/CODEOWNERS` that exists; a path set here that cannot be read is a finding.

allow_unowned.description: A pattern that names no owner is meant (it takes a path out of ownership on purpose), so `data/codeowners-coverage` does not report it.

ignore.description: Gitignore-style patterns of paths that need no owner, such as `*.lock`; `data/codeowners-coverage` does not list them as unowned.

spell.description: The spell pack's options (SR-SPELL decision 7): the locale whose spellings are right, and the words the project accepts, inline and in a words file. Read by the `spell/*` rules. Root config only.

locale.description: `en-US` or `en-GB`: `spell/locale-variant` reports the other locale's spellings (`colour` under `en-US`). Unset, both are accepted and `spell/locale-variant` reports nothing.

words.description: Words the project accepts, compared case-insensitively: never reported by `spell/known-typo`, `spell/known-typo-identifier`, `spell/known-typo-key`, `spell/unknown-word` or `spell/locale-variant`. `spell/suspicious-word` reports an entry that is a known typo.

words_file.description: A file of more accepted words, relative to the config's folder: one word per line, blank lines and lines starting with `#` skipped, merged with `words` and compared the same way. `codelaw spell learn` adds to it and `codelaw init` writes it. Missing at the default path is no error; missing at a path set here is a config error naming it.

todo.description: What a TODO-style comment must carry (SR-CONFIG decision 11a): read by the `*/todo-marker` rules. A written date is enforced whether or not it is required. Root config only.

tags.description: The words that open a marker, at the start of a comment line.

ticket_pattern.description: A regular expression a whole ticket must match.

warn_days.description: A marker is warned about this many days before its date.

commits.description: What a commit message must look like (SR-CONFIG decision 11b): read by `git/commit-message` under `--changed-since`, in the `commit-msg` hook and in the agent hook. Root config only.

preset.description: The convention: `conventional` (`<type>(<scope>)!: <subject>`), `angular`, `gitmoji`, `custom` (the subject line must match `pattern`) or `off`.

types.description: The commit types allowed; Angular's eight under `angular`.

scopes.description: The scopes allowed; empty is any.

subject_max.description: The longest subject line, in characters; 0 is no limit.

subject_case.description: The first letter of the subject: `lower`, `sentence` or `any`.

require_body.description: A body after the subject line is required.

breaking.description: The breaking-change markers accepted: `!` after the type, a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

pattern.description: A regular expression the subject line must match; only with `preset = "custom"`, which requires it.
A regular expression a ticket matches.

place.description: Where the ticket goes: `footer` (any line after the subject), `subject` or `either`.

authors.description: Authors, by name or email, whose commits are not judged.

branches.description: What a branch name must look like (SR-CONFIG decision 11b): read by `git/branch-name` under `--changed-since`. Unchecked until `pattern` is set or a ticket is required. Root config only.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole branch name must match; empty leaves names unchecked.

max_length.description: The longest branch name, in characters; 0 is no limit.

protected.description: Globs of the branches never checked.

skip_authors.description: Authors of `HEAD`, by name or email, whose branches are not checked.

ticket.description: A ticket in the branch name.

pattern.description: A regular expression a ticket matches.

match_commits.description: Every judged commit of the range names the branch's ticket.

pr.description: A pull request's size and description (SR-CONFIG decision 11b): read by `git/pr-size` and `git/pr-description` under `--changed-since`. Root config only.

max_lines.description: Warn above this many changed lines (added plus deleted); 0 is off.

exclude.description: Globs of files not counted: lockfiles and generated files.

title_pattern.description: A regular expression the title must match; empty is any.

require_ticket.description: The title or description names a ticket matching `[commits.ticket]`'s pattern.

template_sections.description: Markdown headings the description must hold, each filled in.

tests.description: Tables about tests (SR-CONFIG decision 11a). Root config only.

skip.description: What a skipped test must carry: read by the `*/skipped-test` rules.

require_reason.description: A reason is required: the framework's own argument, or the text of a `SKIP(…): reason` comment above.

require_expiry.description: A `YYYY-MM-DD` expiry in a `SKIP(…)` comment is required.

ticket_pattern.description: A regular expression a whole ticket must match.

warn_days.description: A skip is warned about this many days before its expiry.

flags.description: Feature-flag expiry (SR-PROJECT-GRAPH decision 11): which calls read a flag, and how its expiry is declared. A `[flags]` table turns on `js/flag-expiry`, `js/flag-marker`, `py/flag-expiry`, `py/flag-marker` and `data/flag-registry`; their flags are registered in `.codelaw/flags.toml` or by inline `codelaw-flag` markers. Root config only.

presets.description: The flag SDKs whose reads codelaw knows: each preset is the SDK's documented read of one flag by its key, for JS/TS and Python.

accessors.description: More calls that read a flag: a pattern with one `$NAME` slot — positional (`isFeatureOn($NAME)`), among others (`flags.get($NAME, $$$)`, `$_` for one argument, `$$$` for the rest), an object key (`useFeature({ key: $NAME })`) or a Python keyword (`flag(key=$NAME)`); `$_.` before the callee matches any receiver. A function whose parameter flows unchanged into an accessor is one too, found through the project graph (`codelaw flags accessors`).

inline.description: `allow`: an inline `codelaw-flag <name> expires <date> owner <owner>` marker registers a flag, and the registry wins when both do. `registry-only`: every marker is an error.

warn_days.description: How many days before its `expires` a flag's reads warn: an integer or a string such as `"14d"` or `"2w"`.

packs.description: Where the engine finds a rule pack (SR-PACK-LOOKUP decisions 6-7). Every key is optional; a key that is set replaces its default and is never added in front of it. Folders are relative to the root config's folder; absolute paths are allowed and no `~` or variable is expanded. Root config only.

order.description: The registries searched for each pack, in this order; a registry left out is not searched.

node_modules.description: The folders that hold npm packages, searched in this order with no walk-up. Unset: `node_modules/` in the config's folder and in every parent folder. A folder set here that does not exist is a config error.

venv.description: One virtual environment whose site-packages are the only Python place; `CODELAW_SITE_PACKAGES` and `$VIRTUAL_ENV` are then ignored. Unset: the launcher's paths, then `$VIRTUAL_ENV`, then `.venv/` in the config's folder. A folder that does not exist, or has no site-packages folder, is a config error.

providers.description: Providers: packages that build a pack's data table from a package installed in the project (SR-RULE-PACKS decision 19). Root config only.

on_missing.description: `skip` (default): the rules and the class sorting that need a provider's table are left out, with one note naming the package to install. `error`: the run stops with exit 2, as for a missing pack.

stylesheet.description: The project's Tailwind CSS stylesheet, relative to the root config's folder. Unset: the first `.css` file under the root that imports "tailwindcss", else Tailwind's own theme.css.

deps.description: The `deps` pack's rules — `deps/vulnerable`, `deps/incomplete-scan`, `deps/outdated`, `deps/stale-snapshot`, `deps/licence`, `deps/lockfile-sync`, `deps/version-drift` and `deps/runtime-agreement` — read against `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, which `codelaw deps refresh` writes from the registries and the advisory sources (SR-RULE-PACKS decision 15). Root config only.

severity.description: The severity of each kind of finding, or `off`: a major, minor or patch version behind, a deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI) version in use, a lockfile behind a range that allows the latest; and a vulnerable dependency by its advisory's severity.

min_release_age.description: Releases younger than this on the snapshot's `fetched` date are not offered: days, or a string like "7d" or "2w".

prerelease.description: Offer prereleases. `deps refresh` keeps them in the snapshot only when this is on.

ignore.description: Packages never reported: `npm:<name>` or `pypi:<name>`, or a table with `package`, an optional `advisory` (then only that advisory, by id or alias, is ignored), an `expires` date (the first day it no longer holds), `added_by` and `reason`.

max_snapshot_age.description: A snapshot older than this on the as-of date is `deps/stale-snapshot`: days, or a string like "14d".

advisory_sources.description: The advisory sources `codelaw deps refresh` reads and merges, the safer answer winning; each on or off. Unset: `registry` (the npm registry and Python index the project already uses), then `osv` at https://api.osv.dev.

npm_url.description: `registry`: the npm registry to ask instead of the one `.npmrc` names.

pypi_url.description: `registry`: the Python index to ask instead of the one the project resolves.

agent.description: What an agent's hooks do with a vulnerable dependency, per advisory severity: `inform` tells the agent the version to move to; `block` also refuses, before it reaches disk, a write that adds one. Never changes a `codelaw check` or CI verdict.

licence.description: `deps/licence`: which licences a dependency may have. `allow` and `deny` are globs over SPDX ids (`*` any run; `GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0` matches a `WITH` id), checked before the defaults, so a configured `allow` lifts a default denial. Defaults: permissive allowed (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, 0BSD, Unlicense, CC0-1.0, PSF-2.0, Python-2.0, BlueOak-1.0.0), copyleft and source-available denied (GPL-*, AGPL-*, LGPL-*, SSPL-*, BUSL-*, EUPL-*), anything else unknown.

unknown.description: The severity of a licence neither allowed nor denied, free text, or none.

ignore.description: Packages whose licence is not judged: `npm:<name>` / `pypi:<name>`, or a table with `package`, an `expires` date, `added_by` and `reason`.

drift.description: `deps/version-drift`: the range a monorepo's workspaces align one dependency to.

policy.description: `highest`: the range whose floor is highest; `root`: the root manifest's, else the highest.

runtime.description: `deps/runtime-agreement`: the place that names the true Node and Python version.

adapters.description: Optional external linters run by `check` and `fix` (SR-LINTER decision 2). Root config only.

enabled.description: The adapters to run when installed; oxlint and Ruff when unset, none when empty.

timeout.description: Per run of an adapter; 60 s by default.

agents.description: Agent surfaces (SR-AGENT-SURFACES decision 6): the agents `codelaw sync-agents` writes files for.

targets.description: The agents whose files `codelaw sync-agents` writes; none by default, and then no agent file exists.

command.description: How hooks and MCP registrations start codelaw; detected from the repo when unset (`npx --no-install codelaw`, `uv run codelaw` or `codelaw`).

reviews.description: The settings of the codelaw-rules-from-reviews skill (SR-AGENT-SURFACES decision 10): which review platform to read and when a repeated review comment becomes a candidate rule. The skill reads them; the engine only validates them and never fetches. Root config only.

platform.description: The review platform, when the git remote does not say: `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket` (Cloud), `bitbucket-datacenter` or `azure` (Azure DevOps). Unset, the skill detects it from the remote's host.

url.description: The base URL of a self-hosted instance (GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab self-managed, Bitbucket Data Center, Azure DevOps Server); needs `platform`. Never a token.

min_repeats.description: How many merged pull requests must carry the same review point before it is proposed as a rule; 3 by default.

min_reviewers.description: How many different reviewers must have made the point; 1 by default, so one reviewer's repeated point counts.

window.description: How far back merged pull requests are read: a whole number and `d`, `w`, `m` (months) or `y`; "6m" by default.

daemon.description: The opt-in warm daemon (SR-ARCHITECTURE decision 22). Root config only.

idle_timeout.description: The daemon exits after this long without a request; 30 minutes (1800 s) by default.

lsp.description: Warm processes' memory bound (SR-ARCHITECTURE decision 24). Root config only.

tree_cache.description: How many closed files' syntax trees a warm process keeps, most recently touched first; open files always keep theirs. 256 by default; 0 keeps none.
